ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, with point C being the midpoint of arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$. If $\angle A=50^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O, $\angle A=50^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle C=180^\circ-\angle A=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ$, \\
since point C is the midpoint of arc BD, \\
$\therefore CD=CB$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBD=\angle CDB$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBD=\frac{1}{2}\times(180^\circ-130^\circ)=\boxed{25^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: From the image, first identify the cyclic quadrilateral with vertices ordered around the circle as B, A, D, C, and note that the target angle ∠CBD is an angle of triangle BCD. From the text, use that ABCD is inscribed in circle O, C is the midpoint of arc BD, and ∠A = 50°. Since ABCD is cyclic, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠BCD = 180° − ∠A = 130°. Because C is the midpoint of arc BD, the arcs BC and CD are equal, so the corresponding chords CB and CD are equal. Thus triangle BCD is isosceles with base BD, giving ∠CBD = ∠CDB. Use the triangle angle sum in triangle BCD to compute each base angle as (180° − 130°)/2 = 25°.
